Rashi on Bava Kamma 50a:10:1.hebrew: לאושין - יסוד לחומת ביתו על פני כל רוחב הבית אצל רה"ר. וחבירו בספר עזרא: "ואשיא יחיטו", ובגמרא: "נפל אשיתא" (ברכות דף נו.):
Rashi on Bava Kamma 50a:10:1.english: For ushin [foundations] - A foundation for the wall of his house across the entire width of the house, next to the public domain. Its parallel [usage] in the Book of Ezra [is]: "and they joined the foundations" [Ezra 4:12], and in the Gemara: "a wall fell" (Berakhot 56a).

Rashi on Bava Kamma 50a:10:2.hebrew: פטור - והיינו נמי כחופר בור ברשותו דאית ליה בעלים והפקיר רשותו, דלא מצי למימר ליה: "מאי בעית ברשותי?" הכא נמי לא מצי למימר ליה: "למה הלכה בהמתך על שפתו?" דהא ברשות הרבים היא:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 50a:10:2.english: Is exempt - And this is also like one who digs a pit on his own property — which has an owner — and declared his property ownerless, where he cannot say to him, "What are you doing on my property?" Here too, he cannot say to him, "Why did your animal walk on its edge?" for it is in the public domain.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 50a:11:1.english: And the reason is that [it is] for foundations - For it is the usual way to do so, and he is not negligent.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 50a:11:2.hebrew: הא לאו לאושין חייב - אלמא בור ברשותו חייב, וקשיא רישא לסיפא:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 50a:11:2.english: But [if] not for foundations, [he is] liable - Thus, [one who digs] a pit in his own domain is liable, and the first clause contradicts the latter clause.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 50a:12:1.hebrew: רישא - דקתני בור ברשותו פטור, ר' ישמעאל:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 50a:12:1.english: The first clause - which teaches [that] a pit in one's own domain is exempt, [follows] Rabbi Yishmael.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 50a:12:2.hebrew: וסיפא - דמיחייב, דדייקינן "הא לאו לאושין חייב", ר"ע:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 50a:12:2.english: And the last clause - where he is liable, as we infer, "but if [it is] not for foundations, he is liable," [follows] Rabbi Akiva.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 50a:13:1.hebrew: אלא לרב יוסף - דאמר בור ברשותו דכולי עלמא חייב, רישא דקתני פטור, מני:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 50a:13:1.english: But according to Rav Yosef - Who said [that regarding] a pit in his [own] domain everyone [agrees he is] liable, the first clause, which teaches [that he is] exempt — whose [opinion is it]?

Rashi on Bava Kamma 50a:14:1.hebrew: לא רשותו ולא בורו - דא"ל: "ברשותאי מאי בעית?". ואצטריך לאשמועי', דאע"ג דאינו רשאי לעשות כן — דאין עושין חלל תחת רשות הרבים — מיהו הואיל ולרשותו פתחו, פטור:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 50a:14:1.english: [Neither] his property nor his pit - For he says to him, "What are you doing in my property?" And it was necessary to teach us [this], because even though he is not permitted to do so — since one may not make a cavity beneath the public domain — nevertheless, since he opened it onto his [own] property, he is exempt.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 50a:16:1.hebrew: דארווח בה ארווחי לרה"ר - דהוה ליה חופר בור ברה"ר, והלכך טעמא דלאושין, הא לאו לאושין חייב:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 50a:16:1.english: Where one widened it into the public domain - For he is [thereby] one who digs a pit in the public domain, and therefore the reason [he is exempt] is [specifically] when [he digs] for foundations, whereas [when it is] not for foundations, he is liable.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 50a:17:1.hebrew: ברה"י הסמוכה לרה"ר - כגון מקצה מקום מרשותו לרשות הרבים, דהוה ליה הפקיר רשותו — פטור:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 50a:17:1.english: On private property adjacent to the public domain - For example, [where] he sets aside a space from his property for the public domain, so that it is [a case of] one who declared his property ownerless — [he is] exempt.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 50a:19:1.hebrew: ומסר לרבים - דאמר לבני עירו: הבור זה שחפרתי צריך לכם לשתות מי גשמים המתכנסין שם, וראויה לשתות בהמות מהן, הרי הוא מסור לכם:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 50a:19:1.english: And transferred [it] to the public - For he said to the residents of his town: This pit that I dug is needed by you to drink the rainwater that gathers there, and [it is] fit for animals to drink from it — behold, it is transferred to you.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 50a:19:2.english: Digger of ditches - For the festival pilgrims on the roads.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 50a:20:1.english: The first hour - For she is still able to remain alive in the water.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 50a:20:2.hebrew: אמר להם שלום - תעלה, וכן שניה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 50a:20:2.english: He said to them: "Peace" - [Meaning] she will ascend, and so too [in] the second [hour].

Rashi on Bava Kamma 50a:20:3.english: The third [hour] - For she would have had time for her soul to depart if she were [still] there.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 50a:20:4.hebrew: אמר להן - כבר עלתה ודאי, כדאמרינן לקמן, דפשיטא ליה דלא תמות שם:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 50a:20:4.english: He said to them - She has certainly already ascended, as we say below, for it was obvious to him that she would not die there.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 50a:21:1.english: A male of ewes - [This was] the ram of Isaac.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 50a:21:2.english: And an old man leading it - Abraham.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 50a:21:3.english: Troubled himself with it - [namely,] to dig pits and caves for the festival pilgrims.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 50a:22:1.english: With those around Him - [The] righteous who cleave to Him.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 50a:22:2.english: It storms [nis'arah] mightily - [This is] an expression [related to] a hairsbreadth [chut hasa'arah].

Rashi on Bava Kamma 50a:22:3.english: And feared by all those that surround Him - [He] casts the dread of His judgments upon them.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 50a:23:2.hebrew: יותרו חייו - יופקרו חייו וגופו, שמורה אל הבריות לחטוא:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 50a:23:2.english: His life will be relinquished - His life and his body will be abandoned, for he teaches people to sin.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 50a:2:1.hebrew: בעל התקלה - ולעולם ברה"ר, אבל ברשותו, אע"פ שהפקיר — פטור, כדפרישית האי דנקט "ולא הפקיר בורו", דאם הפקיר אף בורו הוה ליה בור ברה"ר:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 50a:2:1.english: The one responsible for the hazard - And [this applies] always in the public domain; but on his own property, even though he renounced ownership [of his property], he is exempt — as I explained regarding that which [the Tanna] taught, "and he did not renounce ownership of his pit," for if he had renounced ownership of his pit as well, it would be [considered] a pit in the public domain.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 50a:3:1.hebrew: ומאי זהו דר"ע - בשלמא זהו דרבי ישמעאל למעוטי דר"ע, אלא זהו דר"ע למעוטי מאי? הא בור ברה"ר נמי אמור בתורה, כדדרשינן:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 50a:3:1.english: And what [is meant by] "this is" of Rabbi Akiva - Granted, "this is" of Rabbi Yishmael [comes] to exclude [the view] of Rabbi Akiva; but "this is" of Rabbi Akiva — what [does it come] to exclude? Surely a pit in the public domain is also stated in the Torah, as we expounded.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 50a:3:2.hebrew: לתשלומין - בור דאית ליה בעלים נאמר אצל תשלומין, כדכתיב "בעל הבור ישלם", ובור ברה"ר נאמר אצל הניזקין, כדכתיב "כי יפתח איש וכי יכרה ונפל שמה" וגו'. והכי קאמר ר"ע: אמאי פטרת בבור ברשותו? והלא זהו בור האמור בתורה אצל תשלומין:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 50a:3:2.english: For compensation - A pit that has an owner is stated in connection with compensation, as it is written: "The owner of the pit shall pay," and a pit in the public domain is stated in connection with the damages, as it is written: "When a man opens [a pit], or when [a man] digs [a pit]... and [an ox or a donkey] falls therein," etc. And this is what Rabbi Akiva is saying: Why do you exempt [a person] for a pit on his [own] property? Is this not the [very] pit that is stated in the Torah in connection with compensation?

Rashi on Bava Kamma 50a:6:1.hebrew: הנהו מיצרך צריכי - ולעולם ברשות היחיד והפקיר רשותו ולא בורו, דהוה ליה ממונו שהזיק, חייב משום דקרינן ביה בעל הבור; אבל ברה"ר, דלאו ממונו הוא, פטור:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 50a:6:1.english: These [phrases] are necessary - And in fact, [one is liable only] in a private domain where he renounced ownership of his domain but not of his pit, for it is his property that caused damage — [thus] he is liable, because we apply to him [the phrase] "owner of the pit"; but in the public domain, where it is not his property, he is exempt.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 50a:6:2.english: That he packs [it] - He seals [it] and fills [it with] earth.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 50a:8:1.hebrew: ומאי זהו דר' ישמעאל - הואיל ולדידיה תרוייהו כתיבי:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 50a:8:1.english: And what is "this is" of Rabbi Yishmael - Since according to him both [of them] are written [in the Torah].

Rashi on Bava Kamma 50a:8:2.hebrew: לנזקין - בור ברה"ר פתח בו הכתוב תחלה כשדבר בנזקו, "ונפל שמה שור או חמור" — בור ברשות הרבים דבר בו הכתוב: "כי יפתח" ו"כי יכרה" "ונפל". ואי קשיא: מתני' מני? רבה מוקי לה כר"ע דמחייב אתרוייהו, ורב יוסף מוקי לה כר' ישמעאל:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 50a:8:2.english: For damages - [It is] a pit in the public domain [that] Scripture opened with first when it spoke of its damage, "and an ox or a donkey falls into it" — [it is] a pit in the public domain [that] Scripture spoke of: "if [a man] opens" and "if [a man] digs" [and] "and it falls." And if you ask: Whose [view is] the Mishnah? Rabbah establishes it in accordance with Rabbi Akiva, who holds [one] liable for both [domains], and Rav Yosef establishes it in accordance with Rabbi Yishmael.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 50a:9:1.hebrew: פטור - אם נפל דרך פיו שברשותו, וקס"ד אפילו הפקיר רשותו פטור. אבל אם נפחתה הקמירה שקמר וכסה ברה"ר, חייב, דהאי תנא סבר חיובא דבור ברה"ר הוא:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 50a:9:1.english: Exempt - If [one] fell through its opening that is in his [private] domain, and [we] initially assume [that] even if he declared his domain ownerless, he is exempt. However, if the arch that he arched and covered in the public domain collapsed, he is liable, because this Tanna holds [that] the liability for a pit is [when it is] in the public domain.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 50a:14:1.hebrew: אמר לך רב יוסף כולה דברי הכל היא - לאו דוקא כולה, אלא רישא וסיפא דאקשי מינייהו; אבל מציעתא, דקתני ברה"י ופתחו לרשות הרבים חייב — לא אתיא אלא כרבי ישמעאל:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 50a:14:1.english: "Rav Yosef could have said to you: Everyone agrees with the entire [passage]" - Not literally the entire [passage], rather the first clause and the last clause from which [the Gemara] raised an objection; however, the middle clause — which teaches [that if one digs a pit] in a private domain and opens it to the public domain, he is liable — accords only with Rabbi Yishmael.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 50a:16:1.hebrew: כגון דארווח ארווחי לרה"ר - והשתא כולה דברי הכל: רישא כשלא הפקיר לא רשותו ולא בורו, וסיפא דארווח ארווחי. ומיהו רבי יוסי בר יהודה דבעי הרחקה, לא מתוקמא כרבי ישמעאל:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 50a:16:1.english: For instance, where one widened [the pit] into the public domain - And now, the entire [baraita] is in accordance with all [opinions]: the first clause is when he renounced neither his property nor his pit, and the latter clause is where he widened [the pit into the public domain]. However, [the opinion of] Rabbi Yosei bar Yehuda, who requires distancing [the pit from the public domain], is not established in accordance with Rabbi Yishmael.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 50a:1:1.hebrew: בבור ברשותו - פי' בקונט' דקסבר [ר"י] דכי אפקרינא רשותאי לא ליחייב אנא בהזיקא אפקריניה. משמע דרוצה לומר: אם סמך הבור מתחילה לרה"ר, חייב לכולי עלמא; ואין משמע כן. ועוד, דבסמוך אמר: "הא לאו לאושין חייב", ואוקמה רבה כר"ע, אבל לרבי ישמעאל משמע דפטור. וי"ל דהיינו טעמא משום דא"ל: "תורך ברשותי מאי בעי?" — שלא היה לו להתקרב כל כך אצל רשותי שתפול בבור:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 50a:1:1.english: With a pit in his own property - Rashi explained that [Rabbi Yishmael] holds: "When I renounced ownership of my property, I did not renounce it so that I should become liable for damages." This implies that [Rashi] means to say: if he originally placed the pit adjacent to the public domain, he is liable according to everyone; yet it does not appear so. Furthermore, shortly below [the Gemara] says: "Thus, if it is not for foundations, he is liable," and Rabbah established it in accordance with Rabbi Akiva, whereas according to Rabbi Yishmael it implies that he is exempt. And one can say that this is the reason: because he says to him, "What was your ox doing in my property?" — for it should not have come so close to my property as to fall into the pit.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 50a:21:1.hebrew: דבר שנצטער בו - וא"ת, אכתי מנא ליה? הא מת בנו בצמא! וי"ל דמ"מ באותו דבר עצמו לא היה ראוי ליכשל. בירושלמי (שקלים פ"ה הל"א ע"ש): מלאך בדמות רבי חנינא נזדמן לה:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 50a:21:1.english: "[By] the matter which distressed [that righteous man]" - And if you will ask: Still, how did he know [that she would be saved], for [Neḥunya's] son died of thirst? And one can answer that in any case, through that very matter itself [i.e., a well] it was not fitting for [his offspring] to stumble. In the Yerushalmi (Shekalim 5:1; see there): An angel in the likeness of Rabbi Ḥanina appeared to her.
